column1: # footprint_km is 0 for most rows. Cities of 250k+ get a small radius so they
# beat their own subdivisions and the suburbs ringing them: without it a point
# by Notre-Dame resolved to "Paris 04 Hotel-de-Ville", an arrondissement stored
# as an ordinary populated place with its own population, instead of to Paris.
# population ranks MAP LABELS outside the curated US catalogs, so a domain gets
# its biggest cities first (a Europe map used to come back with no labels at all).
# Country NAMES, not ISO2 codes: half the codes collide with USPS states
# (CA, MO, MD, ME, LA, DE, IN, AL, PA, MT, NE, IL, VA...), so "London, CA"
# would read as California when it means Ontario.
# This work is based on data from GeoNames (https://www.geonames.org/),
# US rows are dropped: us_places_gazetteer.tsv covers the US far more
# densely (all Census places), and two spellings of one city would make
# labels inconsistent. ASCII names (GeoNames `asciiname`) so no glyph is
# missing from the card fonts. Sections of cities (PPLX) and
